name: Abesabesi
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 other work consulted does not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Lau, Jonas. 2021. A Digital Reference Grammar of Abesabesi: Documentation, Description and the Development of a Digital Grammar Format. PhD thesis, Universitaet zu Koeln. kups.ub.uni-koeln.de/35719 (389 pp.)
catalog_locator: Sec. 3.1.5 Tonology, p. 65 (p. 65); typological sketch Sec. 2.1.8 (the text); language identity Sec. 1 (the text)
catalog_quote: Abesabesi has three register tones: a high tone (H) (marked with an acute accent), a mid tone (M) (not marked on vowels) and a low tone (L) (marked with a grave accent). ... The low tone has three different allotones. Following an M, it is produced as a low register tone (see Figure 3.1). Following an H, it is produced as a falling tone, usually starting at a higher pitch than the preceding H (see Figure 3.2). Being the last low tone after one or more consecutive low tones at the end of an utterance, it is produced as an extra low tone (XL) (see Figure 3.3). ... The tone-bearing unit (TBU) is the mora. Light syllables bear one tone, and heavy syllables with long vowels, two vowels, or coda consonants can bear two tones. However, only /j/ and nasal consonants can bear a tone in coda position. The tone borne by a coda consonant can only be L.

tone_statements.citation: Agoyi, Taiwo Opeyemi. 2012. Àbèsàbèsì Orthography: A Proposal. IOSR Journal of Humanities and Social Science (JHSS) 6(2): 41-45. doi:10.9790/0837-0624145
tone_statements.quote: Èsùkù shows evidence of a floating high tone in noun-noun constructions (genitive construction) and declarative sentence( between NP and VP). … Genitive in a noun-noun construction is usually marked by a floating high tone that occurs between the nouns. … A cursory look at the presentation above shows that final vowels of the first noun (N1) in V1 # V2 environment carry mid (i, ii, iii, iv, v, vi, vii, ix, x) and low tone (viii) at the underlying level, but at the surface level they come up with a high tone.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 83-84, section III 3.1 'Floating Tone in Èsùkù', (a) Floating Tone in Genitive Nouns
tone_statements.summary: Marks every vowel high, mid or low (e.g. M-M-M, L-M), no inventory stated; a floating high tone marks genitive N1-N2 and completed action, docking on N1's final vowel as a level high.

tone_statements.citation: Ajao, O. O. 2002. A Generative Phonology of Iyani Akoko. Unpublished undergraduate (B.A.) project, Department of Linguistics and African Languages, University of Ibadan.
tone_statements.quote: The study reveals that Ìkáràm has three basic tones High (H), Low (L) and Mid (M). Contour tones, high-falling and low-rising, are also phonetically realized in Ìkáràm. Tone is a distinctive feature of Ìkáràm phonology and Ìkáràm tones perform both lexical and grammatical functions. … Ìkáràm can be said to be tonal because it has basically three contrastive level tones. … hence, Ìkáràm is a register tone (dialect of a) language. … A contour tone consists of a sequence of two level tones
tone_statements.locator: pp. 15-17: Abstract (p.15), sec. 1.0 Introduction (p.16), sec. 2.3 Contour tones (p.17)
tone_statements.summary: Three contrastive level tones (high, mid, low), lexical minimal pairs and grammatical tone; falling/rising contours are phonetic sequences of two levels; a floating mid tone spreads after deletion.

audit.reasoning: The classification 'tonal' (three register tones H/M/L, TBU = mora, downstep; no word-stress rule stated) rests on a 2021 fieldwork reference grammar that Glottolog ranks as the language's most extensive description, held locally with the deciding passage confirmed verbatim at Sec. 3.1.5, pp. 65-66 (minor locator refinement: the TBU sentences are on p. 66, not 65). A a full-text search for stress/accent confirms the grammar contains no stress/accent statement. All other known descriptive works are 1980s Ilorin student essays on single dialects or Agoyi's vowel-harmony studies, none of which is a prosody source likely to override Lau. no reclassification or re-read needed; at most add 'pp. 65-66' to the locator.
